svg.text: Solana Devnet

g.text: swap_router and fee_bps fixed at creation
a mock Jupiter, fixed at strategy creation

svg.text: the strategy PDA owns all three vaults and is the share mint’s only mint
authority. No handler moves a vault’s tokens to the manager: rebalancing
moves them between strategy-owned vaults, and the fee path mints shares
and touches no vault at all.
an asset is approved if its ApprovedAsset account exists. add_asset() derives
that address for the mint it is handed and fails when the account is missing,
then copies the feed out of it — so a manager can neither list a token they
minted nor pair a real asset with a feed they control.
every deposit deploys fully at the weights, so the USDC vault rests at zero,
and no deposit is accepted until total_weight_bps is exactly 10,000.
deposit() must reference every asset’s accounts at once,
five per asset, so a full sixteen-asset basket runs to 94:
inside Solana’s account-lock limit but far past a legacy
transaction’s size, which is why clients of big baskets
send v0 transactions with an address lookup table.
indexes 0..asset_count are walked whole
or the handler refuses to run: a valuation
that could skip an asset would be a discount
for whoever noticed.
a retired asset keeps its index forever rather than being reused, so the
contiguous range the valuation loop depends on stays intact.
